subject.title: [TUI] Scroll-jump / auto-scroll behavior is still disruptive in 2026.3.8

question: Should disruptive TUI scroll jumps be fixed first by repairing renderer/viewport anchoring, by adding an explicit TUI auto-scroll mode, or by waiting for live reproduction/upstream pi-tui resolution before implementation?
rationale: The source path is credible, but the permanent fix changes terminal UX policy and may require either third-party renderer ownership or a new user-facing TUI mode.

options.title: Repair renderer and anchor behavior
options.body: Prefer a live-proven fix that stops content-driven redraws from clearing or jumping scrollback and follows new output only when the user is already at the tail.

options.title: Add a TUI auto-scroll setting
options.body: Expose explicit terminal user control, accepting the extra settings surface and fresh-install or upgrade proof burden.

options.title: Hold for live repro or upstream
options.body: Keep the tracker open until a current-main terminal capture or upstream pi-tui patch proves the exact repair path.

recommendation.title: Repair renderer and anchor behavior
recommendation.body: Prefer a live-proven fix that stops content-driven redraws from clearing or jumping scrollback and follows new output only when the user is already at the tail.

likelyOwner.reason: They have recent TUI runtime/history work and are closest among the identified owners to the terminal event/rendering path that needs a product-shape decision.
